name: National Seeds Corporation (NSC) Ltd.
about: India's premier government seed company, established under the Ministry of Agriculture. Produces and distributes certified seeds of field crops, vegetables, and fodder crops.
what_they_offer: Certified quality seeds of major field crops (wheat, paddy, oilseeds, pulses, maize, cotton)
how_to_buy: Seeds available at NSC retail outlets, state government seed agencies, and selected dealers. Check website for dealer locator.
note: NSC seeds are government-certified. Look for the tag and batch number on each seed packet to verify authenticity.

name: ICAR Varietal Information
about: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) develops and releases new crop varieties through its network of research institutes. Many high-yielding and disease-resistant varieties originate from ICAR research.
what_they_offer: Research and development of new crop varieties
Information on recommended varieties for different agro-climatic zones
Breeder seed production (supplied to seed companies and state agencies)
how_to_buy: ICAR does not directly sell seeds to farmers. Contact your local State Seed Corporation, KVK, or NSC for seed availability of ICAR-released varieties.
note: ICAR crop variety information is publicly available. Ask your KVK which ICAR varieties are recommended for your district.

name: State Seed Corporations
about: Most Indian states have their own Seed Corporations or Agro-Industries Corporations that supply certified seeds suited to local agro-climatic conditions. These are often the most accessible source of certified seeds for local farmers.
what_they_offer: Certified seeds adapted to local conditions
Often carry ICAR-recommended varieties for the state
Distribution through district and block-level offices
how_to_buy: Contact your District Agriculture Officer or state agriculture department for the nearest seed distribution point. Also available at fair price shops and cooperatives in many states.
contact: Contact your State Agriculture Department or District Agriculture Officer
note: State corporation names vary (e.g., MSSC in Maharashtra, RSSC in Rajasthan, KSSC in Karnataka). Your local agriculture office is the best starting point.

name: Seednet India Portal
about: Seednet India is a central portal for seed supply chain management in India, providing information on certified seed availability, dealer networks, and seed quality standards.
what_they_offer: Seed availability information by crop, variety, and state
how_to_buy: Use the portal to find certified seed dealers in your area. Contact the dealer or your Agriculture Department for purchase.
note: Use Seednet to verify if a seed variety is certified before purchase. This helps avoid counterfeit or uncertified seeds.

name: Seed Quality: What to Look For
about: Tips for verifying seed quality to avoid sub-standard or fake seeds. Each seed packet must have a certification tag to be classified as certified seed.
what_they_offer: Government-certified seeds must have a coloured certification tag (blue for foundation, white for certified grade)
Certification number, lot number, and germination percentage must be on the tag
Buy from authorised dealers or government agencies only
Check expiry date on the seed packet
When in doubt, request germination test certificate from the dealer
how_to_buy: Purchase from authorised seed dealers, state corporations, NSC, or government supply points.
contact: State Agriculture Department or District Agriculture Officer
note: Using certified seeds is one of the most impactful decisions a farmer can make for yield and quality.
